question.text: If the curve, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>y</mi><mfenced><mi>x</mi></mfenced></math> represented by the solution of the differential equation <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></mfenced><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo> </mo><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>, passes through the intersection of the lines, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></math>, then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>|</mo><mi>y</mi><mfenced><mn>1</mn></mfenced><mo>|</mo></math> is equal to ___ .

solution.text:
2xy2-ydx+xdy=0

2xy2dx-ydx+xdy=0

2xdx=ydx-xdyy2=dxy

Now integrate

x2=xy+c

Now point of intersection of lines are 2,1.

4=21+c  ⇒c=2

x2=xy+2

Now y1=-1

⇒|y1|=1
